title: Who Is Oklahoma's Career Rushing Leader? Samaje Perine's 4,122 Yards
question: Who is Oklahoma's all-time leading rusher?
answer: Samaje Perine is Oklahoma's career rushing leader with 4,122 yards from 2014 to 2016, just four yards ahead of Billy Sims (4,118). He took the record in the Sugar Bowl against Auburn on Jan. 2, 2017, and it still stands through the 2025 season.
summary: Samaje Perine is OU's career rushing leader with 4,122 yards (2014-16), four yards ahead of Billy Sims. See the top five and how close the race really was.
body: Oklahoma's career rushing record is one of the tightest races in any school's record book. Samaje Perine holds it with 4,122 yards from 2014 to 2016, and Billy Sims sits second with 4,118. Four yards separate a three-year bruiser from a Heisman legend who played from 1975 to 1979.

The rest of the top five is almost as close. Joe Washington (1972-75) has 4,071 yards, Adrian Peterson (2004-06) has 4,045, and Steve Owens (1967-69) has 4,041. That means only 81 yards separate first place from fifth, a gap smaller than a single good afternoon for any of them.

Perine needed 83 yards to pass Sims entering his final college game, the Sugar Bowl against Auburn in New Orleans. He finished with 86 yards on 17 carries, crossing the mark in the fourth quarter of a 35-19 Oklahoma win. Along the way that night he also passed Washington, Peterson and Owens.

The totals tell different stories about workload. Perine got his yards on 685 carries, Sims on just 593, while Owens needed 958 attempts but scored 57 rushing touchdowns, the most of the group. Just outside the top five are Quentin Griffin (3,938 yards, 1999-2002) and DeMarco Murray (3,685, 2006-10), with Kennedy Brooks (3,320, 2017-21) the leading name from the last decade.
So the next time someone assumes Sims or Peterson owns the record, you have the trivia answer: it belongs to Perine, by four yards.
